subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the centroid of the triangle whose vertices are (5, 4, 6), (1, −1, 3) and (4, 3, 2).

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what the centroid of a triangle is in terms of its vertices, and what you do with each coordinate.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the centroid formula
steps.margin_note: First mark. The centroid of a triangle is the plain average of its three vertices, taken one coordinate at a time. Write the formula before putting any numbers in.
steps.memory_tip: A triangle has THREE vertices, so the centroid divides by 3, not by 2.

recall.must_convey: That the centroid of a triangle is the average of the three vertices, written one coordinate at a time.
accept: the centroid is the average of the three vertices
add the three x values and divide by three, and the same for y and z
write the centroid formula for a triangle first
centroid formula rasi, moodu coordinates average teesukovali
each coordinate of the centroid is its own average
reject: divide by four because there are four points
heard_as: x one plus x two plus x three

steps.why: The centroid formula is one average per coordinate, and the three averages do not interact. Writing the formula first turns the question into three short additions.
common_mistakes: Adding an x value into the y column while working down the list.

steps.label: Substitute and simplify
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Add each column and divide by 3. Only the y column divides exactly, so two of the three answers stay as fractions.
steps.memory_tip: Add down each column, then divide by 3. Keep 10/3 and 11/3 as fractions.

accept: substitute the three vertices and divide each sum by three
the x sum is ten, the y sum is six, the z sum is eleven
the centroid is ten by three, two, eleven by three
substitute chesi moodu tho divide cheyyali
two of the three stay as fractions
reject: the centroid is the average of the vertices

steps.why: Only the middle column divides exactly, so a whole-number answer in all three places would mean an arithmetic slip somewhere in the addition.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign on −1 while adding the y column.
